p_ro has it right -- Grand Jury. This is a body of citizens impaneled by a prosecutor at the state or federal level to hear evidence about an alleged serious crime, then determine whether or not to indict (formally charge) the accused on criminal charges.

If it is indeed true, as you've probably seen mentioned, that there are some 51,000 sealed indictments listed in the federal criminal court system, then that means there has been a grand jury or juries working busily to hear evidence and to hand down indictments on potentially thousands of individuals. (There could be multiple indictments against a single individual, so we can't go by the number of indictments without knowing more.)

Sealed indictments are often kept so (secret) until the accused is arrested and charged. This is often done so that no one can warn the accused and give him or her a chance to flee. (Grand jury proceedings take place behind closed doors.)

There have been rumors that John Huber, the Utah federal prosecutor named by U.S. Attorney General Jeff Sessions to investigate allegations of wrongdoing within the DoJ and FBI, has seated a grand jury of his own. It's possible that this has been true for some time, and that body could already have handed down indictments.

We just don't know yet.
